item.title: Congratulations, PI Toni! A new lab in Granada
item.description: Congratulations to Antonio Herrera Camacho on becoming a Principal Investigator at the University of Granada! Supported by a Ramón y Cajal fellowship, Toni is starting his own independent research group. We are proud to celebrate this milestone with him. Since joining the La Manno Lab in 2021, Toni has brought his experience in developmental biology to our efforts to understand how the brain forms. His work combined embryo culture, spatial transcriptomics, and single-cell analysis, with a particular interest in how folate deficiency affects brain development.

item.title: Gioele wins the Eppendorf & Science Prize for Neurobiology
item.description: We are delighted to celebrate Gioele La Manno’s 2026 Eppendorf & Science Prize for Neurobiology. The prize recognises research on brain lipid diversity, including the Lipid Brain Atlas. This milestone reflects a sustained collaboration across the lab and with Giovanni D’Angelo’s group. Read Gioele’s accompanying essay, “Fats that think?”, in Science, and the official Eppendorf announcement. Thank you to the students, researchers, and collaborators whose work made this possible.

item.title: Thank you and farewell, Francesco!
item.description: We say goodbye to Francesco Danese and thank him for his time in the La Manno Lab. Francesco joined us in August 2025 from Sapienza University of Rome for his master’s thesis. Working with Luca Fusar Bassini, Francesco contributed to our neuroscience knowledge graph project, helping turn information from the scientific literature into structured knowledge that can support biological research. His work brought together machine learning, data science, and the practical challenges of processing a large collection of scientific papers.

item.title: Thank you and farewell, Lothar!
item.description: We say goodbye to Lothar Bezzon, who joined the lab in November 2025 for his master’s thesis research. Working with Gioele La Manno and Luca Fusar Bassini, Lothar explored computational approaches to spatial lipidomics, including the use of independent datasets to benchmark models and test their predictions. Thank you, Lothar, for your contribution to the lab. It was a pleasure to share this stage of your research with you, and we wish you all the best for your next steps!

item.title: Welcome Marco!
item.description: We are happy to welcome Marco Fogli as a postdoctoral researcher in the La Manno Lab. Marco joined the team in 2026, bringing a new colleague to our research community at EPFL. We look forward to working together on the questions that drive our lab: how the brain develops and how its molecular diversity is organised. Welcome, Marco!

item.title: Welcome to our 2026 project students!
item.description: Research visits and student projects are an important part of life in the La Manno Lab. We welcome our 2026 project students: Tecla Duran Fort Mariami Melishvili Laurine Yue Song Shabnam Zareshahraki Thomas van Spaendonk We are glad to have you with us and look forward to the ideas and perspectives you bring to the team.

item.title: Gioele included in the 2026 Stanford/Elsevier top-cited scientists list
item.description: Gioele La Manno is included in the 2026 edition of the Stanford/Elsevier top-cited scientists database, commonly known as the world’s top 2% scientists list. The entry appears in the single-year citation-impact list, based on citations received during 2025, with EPFL as the affiliation and Developmental Biology as the primary subfield. This recognition reflects the continuing use of the lab’s research by the wider scientific community. The database was released on 7 October 2026 using an August 2026 Scopus snapshot.

item.title: Lipid Brain Atlas published in Nature
item.description: Our Lipid Brain Atlas is now published in Nature as “The lipidomic architecture of the mouse brain”. This page first announced the preprint in October 2025 and has been updated for the September 2026 publication. This work, led by Luca Fusar Bassini in collaboration with Giovanni D’Angelo’s lab, reveals that lipids act as zip codes for fine-grained brain anatomy. Key Discoveries Lipizones: A New Way to Map the Brain We discovered lipizones - brain territories defined purely by lipid composition, without any anatomical assumptions.

item.title: MuViT: learning across scales in microscopy
item.description: Congratulations to Albert Dominguez Mantes on MuViT, a CVPR 2026 Highlight paper with Gioele La Manno and Martin Weigert. Microscopy images contain information at many scales. MuViT combines observations at different resolutions, helping a model relate fine structures to their wider tissue setting. Read the conference paper or explore the open-source code.

item.title: Welcome Federica!
item.description: We welcome Federica Schiavetti, who joins us for a master’s valorization project, working with Toni and Evangelia. We look forward to sharing our experimental approaches and working together. Welcome, Federica! Update, November 2026: Federica continues in the lab as a member of our technical staff.

item.title: Lada joins the PhD programme!
item.description: We welcome Lada Polyakova as a PhD student in EPFL’s Computational and Quantitative Biology programme (EDCB). Lada previously visited the lab in 2024 and now returns for her doctoral research. We are happy to continue working together at the interface of computational biology and brain development. Congratulations on this next step, Lada!

item.title: Welcome Lothar!
item.description: We welcome Lothar Bezzon to the La Manno Lab as a visiting master’s thesis student! During his stay, Lothar will work with Gioele La Manno and Luca Fusar Bassini on computational approaches to biological data. We look forward to working together and supporting his master’s research. Welcome to the team, Lothar!

item.title: Antonio Herrera appointed Group Leader
item.description: We are proud to announce that Dr. Antonio Herrera, a postdoctoral researcher in our lab since 2021, has been awarded a prestigious Ramón y Cajal fellowship! During his time in the La Manno Lab, Toni has made fundamental contributions to our research program, including developing computational methods for spatial transcriptomics analysis and contributing to multiple high-impact publications. His work on deep learning methods for imaging and spatial biology has been particularly impactful.

item.title: Welcome Francesco!
item.description: We welcome Francesco Danese, who joins the La Manno Lab from Sapienza University of Rome for his master’s thesis. Francesco will work with Luca Fusar Bassini and Alireza Gargoorimotlagh on computational approaches that connect biological knowledge with single-cell data. His project explores how language models and knowledge graphs can help researchers navigate the scientific literature and formulate questions about existing datasets. We look forward to working together. Welcome to the team, Francesco!

item.title: Congratulations Dr. Irina Khven!
item.description: We are delighted to announce that Irina Khven has successfully defended her PhD thesis! Irina’s thesis, “Fine-grained mapping of neural progenitors subtypes in the embryonic brain unveils context-dependent roles of signalling on cell fate decisions,” represents a major contribution to our understanding of brain development. During her PhD in the EDNE program (2019-2025), Irina made fundamental contributions to mapping neural progenitor diversity using spatial transcriptomics and single-cell approaches. Her work has been instrumental in establishing the lab’s spatial transcriptomics capabilities and generating some of the most comprehensive datasets on embryonic brain development.

item.title: Welcome Laura and Evangelia!
item.description: We are thrilled to welcome two new members to the La Manno Lab! Laura Lapeña Gil joins us as a PhD student in the Neuroscience Program (EDNE) to work on brain development research. Evangelia Skoufa joins as our lab technician, supporting the team with experimental work and laboratory operations including spatial transcriptomics. Welcome Laura and Evangelia!

item.title: Congratulations Dr. Halima Hannah Schede!
item.description: We are delighted to announce that Halima Hannah Schede has successfully defended her PhD thesis! Halima joined as a PhD student in 2020 and completed her thesis jointly supervised with Prof. D’Angelo. Her research focused on computational approaches for spatialomics data: construction, integration, and analysis of biomolecular atlases. She developed Tomographer and made key contributions to the Lipid Brain Atlas project. Halima has accepted a position as Lead Data Scientist at Implexis Ltd in London.

item.title: Congratulations Dr. Alex Lederer!
item.description: We are thrilled to celebrate Alex Lederer’s successful PhD defense! Alex joined the lab as a PhD student in the Computational and Quantitative Biology program (EDCB) in 2019. His research focused on deciphering the nature of cell state transitions in single cells using quantitative modeling of temporal dynamics. His work contributed to major advances in RNA velocity methods, including developments in VeloCycle. Alex has now moved on to become a Senior Data Scientist at CHUV.

item.title: Welcome Xinyi, Morgane, and Alireza!
item.description: We are excited to welcome three new PhD students to the La Manno Lab! Xinyi Huang joins us from the Biotechnology and Bioengineering Program (EDBB) to work on brain development research. Morgane Storey joins as a joint PhD student in the Neuroscience Program (EDNE) between our lab and Prof. Petersen’s lab, working on neuroscience and brain development. Alireza Gargoorimothlag joins from the Neuroscience Program (EDNE) to develop computational approaches for understanding brain development using spatial transcriptomics.

item.title: Luca receives BIF PhD Fellowship!
item.description: Luca Fusar Bassini has been awarded the prestigious Boehringer Ingelheim Fonds (BIF) PhD Fellowship! The BIF PhD Fellowship is one of the most competitive fellowships in biomedical research, with less than 10% of applicants receiving an award. The fellowship supports outstanding junior scientists worldwide who wish to pursue ambitious PhD projects in basic biomedical research in internationally leading laboratories. Luca’s research focuses on the lipidome-transcriptome axis in neurulation and developing computational methods to contribute to therapeutics for neurodevelopmental diseases.

item.title: Welcome Luca and Alessandro!
item.description: Luca Fusar Bassini and Alessandro Valente join the lab for their PhD. Luca is a Biologist with a keen interest in developing computational methods to distill biological insight out of data, Alessandro is Biotechnologist with excellent experience in stem cell engineering and brain organoid models. They are both going to work on the lipidome-transcriptome axis in neurulation. Welcome Luca and Alessandro!.

item.title: Welcome Dimitri!
item.description: Dimitri Lallement joins the lab for a Masters thesis project. He is enrolled in the Computer Science Engineering program, ENSIMAG at Grenoble and doing a exchange with EPFL. He has studied his Bachelor at the University of Bordeaux and studied as Data Scientist Junior at CNES. He wants to face challenging research problem and explore new methods that can help the interpretation of single-cell RNAseq datasets. Welcome Dimitri!

item.title: Welcome Halima!
item.description: Halima Schede joins the lab for a Masters project. She is enrolled in the Bioengineering program and has studied in biology and mathematics at McGill. With her passion for machine learning and neural networks and her knowledge of anatomy and genetics she will turn a bunch of omics data in useful insights of the molecular anatomy of the brain. Welcome Halima!

item.title: Welcome Anurag!
item.description: Anurag Ranjak joins the lab for a Masters project. Anurag is a Chemical Engineer with industry experience in software engineering. He will adventure in spatial transcriptpomics and image reconstruction.He recently “converted” to biology and enrolled in EPFL Masters in Life Sciences. Welcome Anurag!

item.title: Visiting EPFL and super-postdocs in Europe
item.description: Over the last few days I have been at the École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL), Switzerland. The reason of this little trip is that the School of Life Sciences at EPFL recently opened a special position, the fellowship goes under the long name “EPFL Life Sciences Early Independence Research Scholar” shortened “ELIFR fellow”. To explain what an ELIFR fellow is I could simply refer to it as a “super-postdoc”, a funny term popularized by this commentary on Cell but maybe, not yet so popular in Europe (so that I noticed that using it in a conversation often produces raised eyebrows and a grin or two).
